The air hung heavy and cold, smelling of damp earth and decaying leaves. Above, a million pinpricks of starlight pierced the inky blackness, too distant to offer any real illumination in the dense thicket. Each breath felt like a shallow victory, a stolen moment against the throbbing pain that radiated from somewhere deep within. The world swam in and out of focus, a dizzying mosaic of dark shapes and deeper shadows. Getting here… felt impossible now. Moving felt impossible. Staying still felt like an invitation for the cold embrace of the earth to claim you.

A snap. A rustle. Not the wind. Something moving in the woods. Fear, sharp and visceral, cut through the haze of pain. You tried to shift, to find cover, but the effort sent a fresh wave of agony searing through your body. Helpless. Exposed.

Then, a shape emerged from the deeper darkness between the gnarled trees. Tall. Powerful. It moved with a strange, fluid grace, despite a subtle unevenness in its gait, a slight favor of one side. As it drew closer, the faint starlight caught glimpses of it, revealing something utterly alien.

It stopped a few yards away, a dark silhouette against the faint starlight, its form undeniably muscular, broad-shouldered, yet with a distinct curve to the waist. There was a weightiness to its upper body, a rounded prominence beneath its shoulders. Its head was elongated, a strange shape that seemed to warp the space around it.

A soft clicking sound, maybe a limb shifting or armor adjusting. Then, it moved closer still, and the faint light allowed a horrifying clarity.

Its skin was a deep, unsettling purplish hue, almost blending into the night but for a strange, matte texture. And when the lips parted ever so slightly, they revealed rows of sharp, yellow teeth, slightly protruding, like those of a predatory fish.
